name: Pachygyria-Intellectual Disability-Epilepsy Syndrome
aliases: Pachygyria with Intellectual Disability and Epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Pachygyria-Intellectual Disability-Epilepsy Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of pachygyria confirmed by neuroimaging (MRI)
Developmental delay or intellectual disability of variable severity
Recurrent seizures consistent with epilepsy, often refractory
Exclusion of other causes of cortical malformations and epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (pachygyria on MRI, intellectual disability, and epilepsy) must be present
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on neuroimaging and clinical correlation; genetic testing may support diagnosis.

searchTerms: global delay in growth and skills

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; metabolic screening typically unremarkable
imaging: MRI showing pachygyria with thickened, broad gyri and shallow sulci
Possible associated cortical dysplasia or other malformations
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with neuronal migration disorders (e.g., LIS1, DCX) may be identified
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing epileptiform discharges consistent with epilepsy

distinguishingFeatures: More severe smooth brain without gyri (agyria) rather than broad gyri
Excessive small gyri rather than broad gyri
Different seizure types and distribution on imaging
Presence of cortical tubers and subependymal nodules on imaging
Characteristic skin findings and multi-organ involvement

redFlags: Onset of seizures in infancy or early childhood
Severe developmental delay with progressive neurological decline
Refractory epilepsy despite multiple antiepileptic drugs
references: Dobyns WB, et al. Pachygyria and related malformations of cortical development. Neurology. 2019.
Barkovich AJ, et al. Classification system for malformations of cortical development. Neurology. 2012.
